Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:78: So too, whoever conceals his good deeds from people, his reward is that he shall be hidden from the possessors of judgment, for the Holy One, blessed be He, covers him with the garment of Chesed, called "Eloha," so that the possessors of judgment do not recognize him — and this is alluded to in the verse (Job 3:23), "to a man whose way is hidden, whom Eloha has hedged in" — and it is known that the name "Eloha" is the garment for the soul, as it is written (ibid. 29:2), "as in the days of Eloha He watched over me," and as explained in the Sabba [Zohar] (parashat Mishpatim 96b), on the verse (Exodus 21:8), "to a foreign people he shall have no power to sell her, since he has dealt deceitfully with her."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:79: Whoever publicizes that he is fasting is punished, and so the Tashbetz wrote (minor works, siman 111): it is forbidden to publicize to others that one is fasting, and he brought from the Yerushalmi (Chagigah ch. 2, halachah 2), in these words: Rabbi Yosi bar Chanina said, the hinge of the gate of Gehinnom is fixed at his ear. They said to him, why is this so? He said to them, because she was fasting and publicizing it — and some say she fasted one day and it harmed her for two — end of quotation, as pertains here. The intent of "the hinge is fixed" is that the hole passes from ear to ear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:80: Also a great rectification for the penitent is that he strive to observe the Sabbath properly at its entry, and in guarding the Sabbath itself, for all the days nurse from the Sabbath day, as explained in the Zohar (parashat Noach 75b), and as we have elaborated at length in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:81: I saw fit, to complete this chapter, to quote things that lengthen one's days, explained (Ta'anit 20b) regarding fasting: his students asked Rabbi Zeira — and some say, asked Rav Adda bar Ahavah — by what merit have you lengthened your days? He said to them: never in my life did I lose my temper within my own house, nor did I walk before one greater than myself, nor did I contemplate [Torah] in filthy alleyways, nor did I walk four cubits without Torah and without tefillin, nor did I sleep in the study hall, neither a fixed sleep nor an occasional doze, nor did I rejoice at my fellow's misfortune, nor did I call my fellow by a demeaning nickname — and some say, by a family nickname. — end of quotation. Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "chakhinato" — a nickname people give him, such as a descriptive name; "chanikhato" — like the family name in Gittin, up to ten generations (Gittin 88a); and Tosafot explained (Ta'anit 20b, s.v. "bechakhinato") such as up to [family names lasting] ten [generations], such as Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra, whose whole family was called this — and specifically for a demeaning purpose, but for praise it is permitted. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:82: These deeds of Rav Adda bar Ahavah are added to in the Yerushalmi (Ta'anit, ch. 3, halachah 11), in these words: the sages sent and said to him, what good deeds do you have? He said to them: never in my life did anyone precede me to the synagogue; I never left anyone in the synagogue and departed [before them]; I never walked four cubits without Torah; I never mentioned words of Torah in a filthy place; I never lay down and slept a fixed sleep; I never took long strides among my companions; I never called my companion by a nickname; I never rejoiced at my companion's misfortune; my companion's curse never came upon my bed; I never walked in the market near one who owed me money; I never lost my temper within my own house — to fulfill what is said (Psalms 101:2), "I will walk within my house with a whole heart." — end of quotation. There are further several things for length of days, stated in Tractate Megillah (28a) and quoted in Perek Derech Eretz.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:83: Also one should be careful regarding the attribute of truth, whose special property is length of days, as explained in the Gate of Holiness. Also, when the penitent is weak from his fast, especially if he is a Torah scholar and cannot analyze [complex material], he should read at those hours matters of aggadah, which draw the heart, and not sit idle — for one who sits idle from words of Torah is called a scoffer. And the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, wrote regarding the Mishnah (Avot 3:10), "sleep in the morning," etc., in these words: Rabbi Abraham Ibn Ezra, of blessed memory, wrote, there is a way to benefit a weak soul with a difficult halachic matter — one who fears Heaven should fulfill all opinions, and seek for those hours easy matters to understand, so that his conversation not become a cause to distract him from the world and lose what he gained from his analysis. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:84: When the penitent strives to fulfill all these things, Heaven will surely assist him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:1: This chapter shall explain several things a person stumbles in, which are transgressions that a person tramples under his heels, and the penitent must be careful of them so that his repentance be accepted.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:2: The first thing one must be careful of is neglect of Torah, for the punishment for neglecting words of Torah is great, as our sages, of blessed memory, expounded in the Yerushalmi (Chagigah ch. 1, halachah 7), on the verse (Jeremiah 9:12), "and the Lord said, because they have forsaken My Torah": Rabbi Huna and Rabbi Yirmeyah said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak, we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, was lenient regarding idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, and bloodshed, but was not lenient regarding the abandonment of Torah — for "why has the land perished" does not say because of idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, or bloodshed, but rather "because they have forsaken My Torah." Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said, it is written, "and Me they have forsaken" — perhaps [they said] this, but they kept My Torah? For had they forsaken Me but kept My Torah, the light within it would have drawn them close to Me. Rav Huna said, one should study Torah even not for its own sake, for through engaging in it, you will come to do it for its own sake. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:3: Further, in Tanchuma (parashat Re'eh, siman 1), in these words: this is what Scripture says (Jeremiah 21:8), "and to this people you shall say, thus says the Lord: behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death," and it is written (Psalms 78:1), "a maskil of Asaph: give ear, my people, to my Torah, incline your ears to the words of my mouth," and it is written (Deuteronomy 4:9), "only take heed to yourself and guard your soul," etc., and it is written (ibid. 4:10), "the day you stood" — to teach you that whoever neglects Torah is as though he denies the Holy One, blessed be He, for He gave Torah to Israel only so that they engage in it day and night, and it is written (Joshua 1:8), "and you shall meditate on it day and night," etc., and it is written (Psalms 1:2), "but his delight is in the Torah of the Lord," etc. And whoever engages in Torah and fulfills it is as though he received it from Mount Sinai; therefore it is written (Deuteronomy 4:9-10), "and you shall make them known to your children and your children's children, the day you stood," etc. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:4: Whoever is able to engage in Torah and does not is included in "the word of the Lord he has despised" (Numbers 15:31), as we say in Sanhedrin (99a), on the verse "for he has despised the word of the Lord": Rabbi Natan says, this refers to anyone who does not pay attention to the Mishnah. Rabbi Nechemiah says, this refers to anyone who is able to engage in Torah and does not engage. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:5: In the Yalkut on the Prophets (Yalkut, Yehoshua, p. 2, siman 7), it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu: "prepare provisions for yourselves" (Joshua 1:11) — did they then need provisions there? Were they not eating manna, which they gathered every single morning? Rather, he told them thus: repent, so that you may enter the land and eat of the produce of the land, as it is said (Joshua 5:12), "and the manna ceased on the following day." An angel went out to destroy the whole world, saying, the manna has ceased and Torah has ceased [i.e., its study for lack of provisioning need] — as it is said (Joshua 5:13), "and it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho," etc. He said to him [the angel], and how is it, Joshua, that you are wearing shoes, and you do not observe mourning for Israel, that the manna has ceased and Torah has ceased? [Remove] your shoe. Therefore I would say: happy is the man who increases sitting [in study] and labor and diminishes commerce, and sits and meditates on words of Torah every single day continually. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:6: In Eruvin (63a) they said on this matter: "and he said, no, for I am the captain of the host of the Lord" (Joshua 5:14) — he said to him, last night you neglected the evening daily offering, and now you have neglected Torah study! He said to him, for which of these have you come? He said to him, now I have come. Immediately, "and Joshua lodged that night in the midst of the valley" — Rabbi Yochanan said, this teaches that he lodged in the depth of halachic reasoning, etc. And further there, Rav Shmuel bar Abba said in the name of Rav, Torah study is greater than the offering of the daily sacrifices, as it is said, "now I have come." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:7: In the Tikkunim (Tikkun 52, 87a), they said, in these words: woe to human beings who do not engage in Torah, for they are called "dry wood," destined to be burned in the fire of Gehinnom — and it is not for nothing that the masters of the Mishnah said that they toil and inherit Gehinnom. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:8: The reason for all this is that Torah is bound up with His Name, and Torah guides a person to perform the commandments, and the commandments too are bound up with His Name — it follows that whoever does not engage in Torah is as though he denies the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is "he has despised the word of the Lord" — and therefore Gehinnom rules over him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 31:17), "because my God is not within me, these evils have found me," as explained above in the previous chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:9: Besides Torah's function as guidance for performing the commandments, through engaging in it one also attains knowledge of the secret of the supernal Godhead — for this was His intent, blessed be He, in writing the Torah for us with these open and closed passages, and several superfluous and deficient words, because it is an allusion to the supernal Stature [Shi'ur Komah] — and therefore, if even a single letter is missing, it is invalid, since it does not correspond to the supernal pattern.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:10: This is proven in the Zohar (parashat Acharei Mot 71a), in these words: we have learned, Rabbi Yehudah said, one day Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa were walking on the road; they came upon Gush Chalav, which was in ruins, and sat near a burial ground, and Rabbi Yesa had in his hand a torn Torah scroll fragment. While they sat, a certain grave stirred before them and cried out, woe, woe, for the world is in distress, and here is Torah revealed — either the living have come to make us laugh with joy, or with shame, that they shame us with their Torah [errors]. Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa trembled; Rabbi Chizkiyah said, who are you? He said to him, I am dead, and I have been aroused regarding a Torah scroll — for once the world sat in distress, and the living came here to arouse us with a Torah scroll, and I and my companion arrived early at Chevron's resting place; when we joined together in Gan Eden, in the spirit of the righteous, it was found before them that the Torah scroll the living had brought before us was invalid, falsifying the King's name — for an extra vav was found in this verse (Leviticus 11:3), "and cleaves the cleft of hooves" ["u-shosa'at shesa"] — and they said, since they falsified the King's Name, we shall not return to them, and they pushed me and my companion out of the academy at that moment. — end of quotation, the rest of the story not pertaining to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:11: So too it says in the Zohar (parashat Vayechi 225a): but I found one remedy in the world, and no more — in that place where those who labor in Torah are found, and among them is found a Torah scroll not falsified in it — when they take this out, the upper and lower are aroused because of it, and all the more so if the Holy Name is written properly, as we have already taught its matter. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:12: This is the essential completeness in engaging with Torah — to know one's Creator and to cling to Him, etc. — and the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this exposition in the Zohar Chadash on Song of Songs (70b), in these words: "if you do not know, O fairest among women" (Song of Songs 1:8) — it is written (Deuteronomy 4:39), "and you shall know this day and take it to your heart, that the Lord, He is God" — happy are all who engage in Torah to know the wisdom of their Master, and they know and gaze into supernal secrets — for when a person leaves this world with this, all the world's judgments are removed from him, and moreover thirteen gates of the secrets of pure balsam are opened for him, in which the secrets of supernal wisdom depend, and moreover the Holy One, blessed be He, engraves him upon that royal robe on which all patterns are engraved, both in this world and in the World to Come, and the Holy One, blessed be He, delights in him in the Garden of Eden, and he inherits two worlds — this world and the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:13: The wisdom a person needs is to know and gaze at everything through the secret of his Master — one, to know and gaze at the secret of his Master; and one, to know his own body, and to know who he is, and how he was created, and from where he comes, and to where he goes, and how the rectification of the body is to be rectified, and how he is ready to enter into judgment before the King of all; and one, to know and gaze at the secrets of his soul — what is that soul within him, and from where does it come, and for what purpose does it come into this body, a foul drop, here today and tomorrow in the grave; and one, to gaze at this world in which he is, and for what purpose it is arranged, and afterward at the secrets of the world above, to know his Master — and all this a person contemplates within the secrets of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:14: Come and see, whoever goes to that world without knowledge, even if he has many good deeds, is expelled from all the gates of that world. Go out and see what is said there: tell me the secrets of wisdom that I do not know and have not learned until now, so that I not be shamed among those supernal grades I am entering, for until now I have not gazed at them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:15: Come and see, what is written: "if you do not know, O fairest one" — if you come without knowledge, and have not gazed at wisdom before you enter, and do not know the secrets of the supernal world — go out, you may not enter here without knowledge. — end of quotation, as pertains here, the rest of the verse being explained there in the manner mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:16: With this one may understand what our sages, of blessed memory, said in Tanchuma, that the verse (Jeremiah 9:23), "but let him who glories glory in this: that he understands and knows Me" is said regarding Torah, in these words: and how does a person glory in this world? Through the crown of Torah, which enriches him and gives him life in this world and in the World to Come, as it is said (Proverbs 3:16), "length of days is in her right hand, in her left hand riches and honor" — and gives him strength that shall never fail, as it is said (Isaiah 40:31), "but those who hope in the Lord shall renew their strength." — end of quotation. And this is because Torah is called "zot" [this], as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:44), "and this is the Torah which Moses set." And the conclusion of the verse, "understands and knows Me," indicates that through Torah we come to know Him, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:17: Because "the beginning of strife is like letting out water" (Proverbs 17:14), as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Kiddushin 40b), that a person's first judgment concerns whether he engaged in Torah, therefore the beginning of repentance must be to engage in Torah, for study leads to action. Therefore we say in our prayer, "return us, our Father, to Your Torah," and afterward, "and draw us near to Your service."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:18: When he engages in Torah for its own sake — namely, to study and to do, as explained in the introduction to this book — the secrets of Torah will be revealed to him, as Rabbi Meir said (Avot 6:1), whoever engages in Torah for its own sake merits many things, etc., and the secrets of Torah are revealed to him, and he becomes like an overflowing spring. And likewise through repentance, as it is written (Proverbs 1:23), "turn at my rebuke; behold, I will pour out my spirit to you, I will make my words known to you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:19: Further, he should examine whether he has transgressed one of the twenty-four things for which one is excommunicated, which Maimonides wrote in the Laws of Torah Study, and these are: (1) whoever demeans a sage, even after his death; (2) whoever demeans an agent of the court; (3) whoever calls his fellow "slave"; (4) whoever belittles a single matter of the words of the scribes, needless to say a matter of the Torah itself; (5) whoever is summoned by the court and given an appointed time, and does not come; (6) whoever does not accept the verdict [of the court] — they excommunicate him until he pays; (7) whoever has in his possession something that causes damage, such as a vicious dog or a rickety ladder — they excommunicate him until he removes the hazard; (8) whoever sells his land to a gentile — they excommunicate him until he accepts upon himself [liability for] any compulsion the gentile brings against his fellow Israelite, the owner of the adjacent boundary; (9) whoever testifies against a fellow Israelite in gentile courts, and money is extracted from him through his testimony unlawfully — they excommunicate him until he pays; (10) a slaughterer who does not separate the priestly gifts and give them to a priest — they excommunicate him until he gives them; (11) whoever desecrates the second day of festivals of the Diaspora, even though it is [only] a custom; (12) whoever performs labor on the eve of Passover after midday; (13) whoever mentions the Name of Heaven in vain, or in an oath over idle matters; (14) whoever brings the multitude to eating sacred things outside [their proper place]; (15) whoever brings the multitude to a desecration of the Name; (16) whoever calculates years and fixes months outside the Land of Israel; (17) whoever causes the blind to stumble; (18) whoever prevents the multitude from performing a commandment; (19) a slaughterer from whose hand a treifah [invalidly slaughtered animal] emerged; (20) a slaughterer who did not show the inspection of his knife to a sage; (21) whoever brings himself to erection deliberately; (22) whoever divorces his wife and then forms a partnership with her, or business dealings that bring them to associate with one another — when both come to judgment, they are excommunicated; (23) a sage of ill repute; (24) whoever excommunicates one who is not liable to excommunication.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:20: They explained in the Zohar (parashat Pekudei 249b) that in the Hall of Nogah there are four angels with several companies who excommunicate those who defile their mouths, and likewise all those who have sinned sins requiring rebuke — ten proclamations go forth each day, proclaiming throughout all those firmaments and among all those hosts and camps: beware of so-and-so, who is under rebuke — the rebuke being for such-and-such a sin that so-and-so committed, until he returns before his Master, may the Merciful One save us. When he returns from that sin, these [angels] gather and release him, and then they proclaim, so-and-so's rebuke is released; from now on his prayer enters. But until he returns, he is under rebuke above and below, and his Master's protection is removed from him, and even at night his soul is under rebuke, for all the gates of heaven are closed to it and it does not ascend, and it is pushed outward. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:21: Therefore one must examine his deeds to see if he has sinned in one of these matters, particularly if he has brought himself to erection deliberately, which is common among unmarried young men — he must accept rebuke upon himself, and sit on the ground as one excommunicated and wrapped [in mourning]. So too we find that David accepted rebuke upon himself, as explained above (ch. 3), and so our sages, of blessed memory, explained in Midrash Yalkut (Shmuel, siman 95, p. 15d, and also Midrash Tadshe there).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:22: Further, if he sinned with his limbs, he should perform commandments with them — this matter is explained in Midrash Yalkut (Judges, remez 42): all the tribes established judges and kings, but the tribe of Simeon, because it sinned in licentiousness, established neither judge nor king; and it says afterward, therefore the covenant of circumcision was given in the private organ, so that fear of the Omnipresent might restrain one from committing that sin. For each and every sense the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Torah teaching what to do and what not to do: for the heart — "and you shall not go astray after your heart and after your eyes" (Numbers 15:39); for the ears — "you shall not accept a false report" (Exodus 23:1); for the mouth — "you shall not eat any abomination" (Deuteronomy 14:3); for the tongue — "you shall not take the Name of the Lord" (Exodus 20:7), "you shall not swear falsely" (Leviticus 19:12), "you shall not lie" (ibid. 19:11); for the hands — "do not put your hand with the wicked" (Exodus 23:1); for forbidden relations — "you shall not commit adultery" (Exodus 20:13), "you shall not commit harlotry"; for the feet — "you shall not go after other gods" (ibid. 20:3) — all of these are negative commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:23: And what to do — this teaches, for the heart: "and you shall place these My words upon your heart" (Deuteronomy 11:18); for the eyes: "lest you forget the things your eyes have seen" (ibid. 11:12, adapted); for the ears: "hear, O Israel, the statutes" (ibid. 5:1); for the tongue: "and you shall teach them diligently to your children" (ibid. 6:7); for the hands: "you shall surely open your hand" (ibid. 15:8); for forbidden relations: "and you, be fruitful and multiply" (Genesis 9:7), and it says (Jeremiah 29:6), "take wives and beget [children]"; for the feet: "you shall walk in all the way that the Lord your God has commanded you" (Deuteronomy 5:30). — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:24: Likewise, if he sinned in a sin that many stumbled in, he must give merit to the multitude through his own deeds — and so they said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu, in the Yalkut, parashat Ki Tissa, in the passage of the golden calf, in these words: Aaron himself knew that a great matter had come upon Israel through him, and he stood and bound an iron rope around his loins, and went about among all the camps of Israel — whoever did not know how to pray, he taught him prayer; whoever did not know how to recite the Shema, he taught him the Shema; whoever was not versed in the body of Torah, he brought him into the body of Torah. Not Aaron alone, but whoever teaches Torah publicly to Israel for the sake of Heaven, the Omnipresent has mercy on him and gives him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and intellect, and gives him his portion with the three patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:25: Every penitent must teach the ways of repentance to whomever he knows has sinned, especially if that person is accustomed to him and will accept his words, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 51:15), "I will teach transgressors Your ways." On the merit of one who brings a wicked person back to repentance, many merits are explained in the Zohar (parashat Terumah 128-129).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:26: Further, one must be careful of all aspects of theft; besides monetary theft there is another kind of theft. They said in Tractate Berachot (6b): Rav Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna, whoever knows that his fellow is accustomed to greet him should greet him first, as it is said (Psalms 34:15), "seek peace and pursue it"; and if his fellow greeted him and he did not return the greeting, he is called a robber, as it is said (Isaiah 3:14), "and you have consumed the vineyard, the plunder of the poor is in your houses." — end of quotation. Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "the plunder of the poor" — but is not the plunder of the rich also plunder? Rather, the plunder of the poor man is that he has nothing else to be robbed of except the failure to return his greeting.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:27: Further, he should be careful not to benefit from any worldly thing without a blessing, for one who does so is called a robber, as we learn in Berachot (35b): Rabbi Chanina bar Papa said, whoever benefits from this world without a blessing is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Assembly of Israel, as it is said (Proverbs 28:24), "whoever robs his father and mother, and says, it is no transgression, is a companion of a destroyer" — and "his father" refers only to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:6), "is He not your Father who acquired you"; and "his mother" refers only to the Assembly of Israel, as it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "hear, my son, the discipline of your father, and do not forsake the Torah of your mother." What is "a companion of a destroyer"? Rabbi Chanina bar Papa said, he is a companion of Jeroboam son of Nevat, who destroyed Israel before their Father in Heaven. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:28: Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "robs the Holy One, blessed be He" — of His blessing; "and the Assembly of Israel" — for when they sin, the fruits are afflicted. "No transgression" — and because he treats it lightly, others see and learn from him to do the same, to benefit from this world without a blessing, and therefore this one who treats it lightly is called a companion of a destroyer, of Jeroboam son of Nevat, who sinned and caused others to sin — so this one sins and causes others to sin. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:29: Above, in chapter 2, we explained that even one who does not engage in Torah and commandments properly is called a robber, especially in this our exile, when the Shechinah is in exile because of our sins, as it is said (Isaiah 50:1), "and because of your transgressions your mother was sent away" — and she has no rest and no union except through us, when we engage in Torah and commandments, and whoever does not engage is called a robber. And they said in the Zohar, parashat Vayeshev (191b), whoever does not gaze at the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, causes the Shechinah to be subdued in the dust, in the manner of (Isaiah 26:5), "He brings low, He lays it low, even to the ground," etc. And likewise they said in parashat Va'etchanan (268a), which we quoted in the Gate of Love (ch. 8), that whoever prevents himself from engaging in Torah is as though he withheld from the Shechinah her food, clothing, and conjugal rights.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:30: Now, in exile she is called a widow, as it is said (Lamentations 1:1), "she has become like a widow," and the Righteous One [Tzaddik] is the orphan; therefore the Torah commanded (Exodus 22:21), "you shall not afflict any widow or orphan" — and our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Mechilta DeRashbi), even the widow of a king — and in exile she is the widow of the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, so to speak, and one must not afflict her judgment; likewise, one must perform the unifications pertaining to the Righteous One and not afflict his judgment. "For if you afflict him at all" [doubled verb] indicates the plain and hidden meaning, the lower orphan and the lower widow, and the supernal allusion we explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:31: Further, one must be careful of fraud [ona'ah], even fraud through words, and fraud through words is harsher than monetary fraud, as explained in Bava Metzia (58b), and it says there, three [sins], the curtain [before God] is never closed against them: fraud, theft, and idolatry. Fraud, as it is written (Amos 7:7), "behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made with a plumb-line [anach], with a plumb-line in His hand" — [connecting "anach" to "ona'ah"]. Theft, as it is written (Jeremiah 6:7), "violence and plunder are heard continually before Me." Idolatry, as it is written (Isaiah 65:3), "a people who provoke Me continually to My face." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:32: Further, one should be careful of these four things, one who does any of which is called wicked. They said in the Pesikta (Rabbati, addition 1, parashah 4): three are called wicked — one who raises his hand against his fellow, as it is said (Exodus 2:13), "and he said to the wicked one, why do you strike your fellow"; a person of contention, as it is said (Numbers 16:26), "depart now from the tents of these wicked men"; and one who borrows and does not repay, as it is said (Psalms 37:21), "the wicked borrows and does not repay." Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Tanchum said, Rabbi Tanchuma said to me, also one who is brazen-faced, as it is said (Proverbs 21:29), "a wicked man hardens his face." — end of quotation.
